core_obligations: Identify the strict henselisations (proof lines 19310-19322): for geometric points t' of Spec(O^sh_{S',s'}) and its image t, the quasi-finiteness (or inverse limit, or integrality) assumption on g together with the algebra lemma makes the natural map O^sh_{X,x} tensor_{O^sh_{S,s}} O^sh_{S',s'} -> O^sh_{X',x'} an isomorphism.

Identify the varieties of vanishing cycles (proof lines 19323-19338): since the residue fields of t and t' agree, the displayed chain of equalities shows F_{x',t'} = F_{x,t} as the spectra of the corresponding tensor products of strict henselisations with the residue field.

Conclude (proof lines 19339-19344): hence the varieties of vanishing cycles of f' at x' are among those of f at x, so the vanishing hypothesis for f gives the same vanishing for f' relative to (g')^{-1}K, which is local acyclicity at x'.
proof_roadmap: Compare the strict henselisations along the base change, using the quasi-finiteness hypothesis.
Identify the varieties of vanishing cycles of f' with those of f.
Transport the vanishing that defines local acyclicity of f to f'.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the stability of local acyclicity under base change by a quasi-finite morphism (or an affine inverse limit of quasi-finite schemes, or an integral morphism) (statement lines 19288-19307). The proof (proof lines 19309-19344) identifies the strict henselisations along the base change through the algebra lemma, deduces the equality F_{x',t'} = F_{x,t} of varieties of vanishing cycles because the residue fields agree, and reads off local acyclicity of the base change from that of f. H2: one strict-henselisation comparison followed by the identification of the vanishing-cycle varieties.
